researcher_notes: 4 PDFs processed: three print-to-PDF captures of agilox.net product pages (Agilox One.pdf, Agilox OFL.pdf, Agilox ODM.pdf — nav bar 'SOFTWARE PRODUKTE UNTERNEHMEN KARRIERE BLOG KONTAKT DE' captured, single page, no page numbering) and one real 20-page corporate brochure (agilox-corporate-folder-o-de_02_2026_web.pdf, dated '02/2026 Druckfehler und Änderungen vorbehalten.' on p.20). A fifth file in the folder, 'AGILOX  OCF.html', is not a PDF and was left untouched per instruction — so the OCF entry below is sourced ONLY from the corporate folder. The brochure's p.17 is a full four-product comparison matrix (ONE(+NFK) / OFL / OCF / ODM, with ODM occupying TWO columns for the 600 and 800 fork lengths) and is the single most valuable page in the whole AGILOX set. It was verified by rendering at 150 dpi with pdftoppm because pdfplumber's plain text linearisation mis-attached the '(geschl.)' qualifier from the OCF column to the OFL column — the render shows OFL = 'Palette 1.200 x 800 mm' and OCF = '(geschl.) Palette 1.200 x 1.200 mm'. TERMINOLOGY WARNING that governs this whole group: AGILOX distinguishes MIN. DURCHFAHRTSBREITE (pass-through width, a one-off gap the vehicle must squeeze through) from MIN. GANGBREITE (working aisle width) — and these differ by 200-400 mm. The ODM PRODUCT PAGE conflates them: it prints 'MIN. GANGBREITE 1.000 MM' where the brochure's matrix says ODM 600 Durchfahrtsbreite = 1.000 mm and Gangbreite = 1.300 mm. The brochure matrix is the authority. AP0's min_aisle_width hint maps to GANGBREITE. IMPORTANT NON-FINDING: min_turning_radius = 0 on the existing AMR rows is CORRECT, not a Blank-vs-Zero bug — the AP0 hint says literally '(0 if omnidirectional)' and every AGILOX vehicle is omnidirectional. Correspondingly, AGILOX's published DREHKREIS figures are turning-CIRCLE DIAMETERS (the brochure p.16 diagram labels 'G Drehkreis' as a full circle) and must NOT be written to min_turning_radius. Nothing was mapped from them.

products.notes: CONFLICT — min_aisle_width: the DB row holds 1300 mm. That is wrong on TWO counts. (a) SCOPE: min_aisle_width exists only in Logistics:AGV:Forklift and Logistics:AGV:Tugger scope; this row is Mobile AMR, so the field should not be populated here at all. (b) VALUE: brochure p.17 gives ONE a MIN. GANGBREITE of 1.600 mm and a MIN. DURCHFAHRTSBREITE of 1.400 mm — 1300 matches neither, and is in fact the ODM 600's Gangbreite. Looks like a cross-product copy error. CONFLICT — charge_time: the DB holds 3 (minutes). Agilox One.pdf's row reads 'LADEZEIT — 3 Minuten laden = 1 Stunde Betrieb', which is a charge-to-runtime RATIO, not a time-to-full. AP0's charge_time is 'Integer min' to charge; 3 minutes to full charge is not what the source says. Contrast the ODM page, which states a real one ('20 – 100 % in ca. 11 Min.'). products.notes: VARIANT-COMPLETION FINDING — this variant is absent from the DB. Agilox One.pdf's TECHNISCHE DETAILS table has TWO columns (EINFACHSCHERENHUB / DOPPELSCHERENHUB) and the DB holds only the single-scissor figures (max_payload 1000, lift_height 620). The double-scissor is a materially different machine on two hard K.O. fields: it lifts 1.100 mm instead of 620 mm (nearly double) but carries only 750 kg instead of 1.000 kg. A tender needing 1 m of lift currently matches no AGILOX ONE at all. Note the payload/lift trade-off runs in OPPOSITE directions, so neither variant dominates the other — this is exactly the case where collapsing to one row loses real matching capability. Whether this becomes its own Product row or a second Base Model under a shared ONE base is the import author's call; the chassis is provably shared (identical dimensions and tare weight). Corridor geometry is identical to the standard ONE (brochure p.17 column 'ONE (+NFK)' is not split by lift variant): DREHKREIS 2.100 mm, MIN. GANGBREITE 1.600 mm, MIN. DURCHFAHRTSBREITE 1.400 mm — none storable in AMR scope. Cleanroom Klasse 6 and the full load-carrier list from the ONE page apply equally but were not duplicated here; apply the standard ONE's values.

products.notes: CLASSIFICATION QUESTION FOR THE TECH LEAD — the DB carries AGILOX NFK as a standalone product with max_payload 1000 and lifting_height 620 (i.e. the plain ONE's Einfachscherenhub figures). Both 2026 documents treat NFK as an ACCESSORY of the ONE, not a model: brochure p.10 lists it under the ONE's option bullets ('NFK – Narrow Fork: Monogabel für schmale Ladungsträger', alongside GABELN, BCO and REINRAUM), and the p.17 comparison matrix has no NFK column at all — its column is headed 'ONE (+NFK)', i.e. one set of numbers covering both. So either (a) NFK should be merged into AGILOX ONE as a fork option, or (b) it stays as a variant row but must be understood as sharing the ONE base model entirely. Nothing in the corpus supports it as an independent machine with its own geometry. Note the existing row also stores lifting_height = 620, which is a FORKLIFT-scope field on a Mobile AMR row (the AMR-scope equivalent is lift_height) — a wrong-scope value regardless of how the merge question is decided. No new numeric values are proposed here beyond the shared envelope, because the documents publish none specific to the NFK.

products.notes: CONFLICT — min_aisle_width, and it is the most consequential finding in the AGILOX group: the DB holds 1300 mm; brochure p.17 states 2.100 mm for the OCF. An 800 mm gap on a hard K.O. (KO_IF_GT) field, in the direction that makes the OCF look FAR better than AGILOX claims — it would currently pass narrow-aisle tenders it cannot physically serve. The DB's 1300 is exactly the ODM 600's MIN. GANGBREITE from the same matrix row, and the identical 1300 also sits on the AGILOX ONE row (whose true figure is 1.600 mm), so this looks like one cross-product copy error propagated to two rows. Note also that 1300 is not even the OCF's narrowest published number — its MIN. DURCHFAHRTSBREITE is 1.700 mm. NOTE ON SOURCING: this entry is built from the corporate brochure ONLY. The dedicated OCF document in the folder is 'AGILOX  OCF.html', which is not a PDF and was left untouched per instruction — it should be processed separately, and it very likely carries the Hubhöhe/Hubkapazität figures the brochure withholds. lifting_height NOT PROPOSED, flagged instead: the DB holds 1600 mm; the brochure publishes only 'MAX. The DB's existing 6-value load_type list is not contradicted and was left alone. NOT MAPPED: DREHKREIS 3.500 mm (diameter), overall height 2.566 mm, MIN. DURCHFAHRTSBREITE 1.700 mm, IDEALE GANGBREITE 2.700 mm, GEGENVERKEHR 3.200/3.800 mm, PARALLEL 3.200 mm, ABSTAND BLOCKLAGER 100/200 mm. products.notes: CONFLICT — the ODM PRODUCT PAGE mislabels its own aisle figure, and this is a trap for any future re-extraction. Agilox ODM.pdf prints 'MIN. GANGBREITE 1.000 MM (35 in)', but brochure p.17 assigns 1.000 mm to MIN. DURCHFAHRTSBREITE and gives MIN. GANGBREITE = 1.300 mm for the ODM 600. AGILOX's own p.16 diagram distinguishes the two (marker A = Durchfahrtsbreite, marker B = Gangbreite). The brochure matrix is the authority; the product page's label is wrong. Neither figure is storable anyway (Mobile AMR has no aisle field), but a reviewer reading only the product page would record a 300 mm-too-narrow aisle. CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE BROCHURE (recorded, not resolved) — the ODM's DREHKREIS is given as '1.700 / 1.900 mm (66,9 in / 74,8 in)' on p.13 and as '1.300 mm / 1.600 mm' on p.17 row G. Agilox ODM.pdf independently says 1.700 MM (67 in), so 2 of 3 statements say 1700 for the ODM 600. Geometry mildly favours the p.17 figure (the vehicle's circumscribed circle is sqrt(1095^2+400^2) = 1166 mm), but the loaded swept circle would be larger. No AP0 field is affected — Drehkreis is a diameter and min_turning_radius is correctly 0 for an omnidirectional vehicle — so this is reported for completeness only. VARIANT SPLIT PROPOSED: see the sibling 'AGILOX ODM 800' entry. The existing merged row 'AGILOX ODM 600/800' currently carries the 600's numbers only. STATION HEIGHT 0: the headline stat block reads '0 mm — maximale Stationshöhe' (also brochure p.13). That is a genuine printed zero meaning floor-to-floor only ('Boden-zu-Boden' on p.7), NOT a missing value — worth stating explicitly because it is the one place in this batch where 0 is real. It does not conflict with lift_height = 250 mm, which is the stroke used to pick the dolly up off the floor. DB CLEANUP: load_type is stored as 'Roll Container|Custom Carrier (dolly)' — the parenthetical '(dolly)' makes it a non-conforming allowed value. NOT MAPPED: overall height 1.235 mm, tare weight 160 kg, fork width 205 mm ('Mit einer 205 mm breiten Gabel'), ABSTAND BLOCKLAGER 0/50 mm, ABSTAND EINZELSTATIONEN 50 mm. ADD-ONS also listed: OBSTACLE AVOIDANCE ('Zusätzliche 3D-Sensorik in Fahrtrichtung zur Erhöhung der Sicherheit im Mensch-Maschine-Mischumfeld') and PLUG & PERFORM ('Implementierung unserer AMRs in weniger als 12 [Stunden]'). The Obstacle-Avoidance wording matters for safety_coverage across the range: the 3D sensing is an ADD-ON on the ODM and ONE pages, whereas the OFL page presents it as fitted.

products.notes: VARIANT-COMPLETION FINDING — the DB's single row 'AGILOX ODM 600/800' carries only the 600's geometry. The 800 is a genuinely different footprint: 1.295 mm long vs 1.095 mm (+200 mm) and it carries an 800 x 600 mm dolly instead of a 600 x 400 mm one. Its corridor requirements are correspondingly wider throughout brochure p.17: MIN. DURCHFAHRTSBREITE 1.200 vs 1.000 mm, MIN. GANGBREITE 1.600 vs 1.300 mm, IDEALE GANGBREITE 2.100 vs 1.800 mm, GEGENVERKEHR 1.900/2.800 vs 1.700/2.500 mm, PARALLEL 1.800 vs 1.700 mm. NONE of these is storable — Mobile AMR has no aisle-width field in AP0 — which means that after import the ODM 600 and ODM 800 would be distinguishable ONLY by vehicle_length. That is the strongest concrete argument encountered so far for adding an AMR-scope aisle-width field: without it, the split arguably is not worth doing. Payload, lift height, speed, cleanroom class and all navigation/safety attributes are identical to the 600. DREHKREIS is reported as 1.900 mm on p.13 and 1.600 mm on p.17 (same intra-document contradiction as the 600) — not mapped either way, since it is a diameter and min_turning_radius is 0 for omnidirectional vehicles.
